Fuzzy left join including a jon specification on a date

Source: R/join.R
clr_left_join_fuzzy_date.Rd

Fuzzy left join including a jon specification on a date

Usage

clr_left_join_fuzzy_date(
  x,
  y,
  by_date_x,
  by_date_y = by_date_x,
  by_not_fuzzy = NULL,
  suffix = c(".x", ".y"),
  num = 1,
  units = "days"
)

Arguments

x, y

A pair of data frames, data frame extensions (e.g. a tibble), or lazy data frames (e.g. from dbplyr or dtplyr). See Methods, below, for more details.

by_date_x, by_date_y

A join specification with the name of the date variable of dataset x & y invalved in the fuzzy date join. If only by_date_x is provided, by_date_y will default to by_date_x.

by_not_fuzzy

A regular join specification.

suffix

If there are non-joined duplicate variables in x and y, these suffixes will be added to the output to disambiguate them. Should be a character vector of length 2.

num

a numeric or character vector. A character vector can specify periods in a convenient shorthand format or ISO 8601 specification. All unambiguous name units and abbreviations are supported, "m" stands for months, "M" for minutes unless ISO 8601 "P" modifier is present (see examples). Fractional units are supported but the fractional part is always converted to seconds.

units

a character vector that lists the type of units to be used. The units in units are matched to the values in num according to their order. When num is character, this argument is ignored.

Value

An object of the same type as x (including the same groups), with the same number of rows as x. The order of the rows and columns of x is preserved as much as possible.

Examples

clr_left_join_fuzzy_date(
data.frame(
  id = 1:5,
  sexe = c("F", "H", "F", "F", "H"),
  date_nais = c("1923/01/01", "1924/01/01", "1925/01/01", "1926/01/01", "1927/01/01") %>%
  lubridate::ymd(),
  DB = c("oui", "non", "non", "oui", NA_character_)
),
data.frame(
  id = 1:5,
  sexe = c("F", "H", "F", "F", "H"),
  date_nais = c("1923/01/01", "1924/01/02", "1924/12/31", "1926/01/03", "1926/12/30") %>%
  lubridate::ymd(),
  DB = c("oui", "non", "non", "oui", NA_character_)
), by_date_x = "date_nais", by_not_fuzzy = "id"
)
#>   id sexe.x date_nais.x DB.x sexe.y date_nais.y DB.y
#> 1  1      F  1923-01-01  oui      F  1923-01-01  oui
#> 2  2      H  1924-01-01  non      H  1924-01-02  non
#> 3  3      F  1925-01-01  non      F  1924-12-31  non
#> 4  4      F  1926-01-01  oui   <NA>        <NA> <NA>
#> 5  5      H  1927-01-01 <NA>   <NA>        <NA> <NA>
